opening_line: The thin gold frame around the hero on the Acadia Building Co. site pulls its color straight from their logo and tree mark, so the photo, the type and the brand read as one piece.
Cropping the Dunlavy speakers huge and tilted on pure black was the right call. The cabinets carry the whole first screen and the copy stays out of their way.

Leading the Silicon Ranch homepage with sheep grazing under the panels, toned down in that navy wash, is a smart photo choice. It explains what kind of solar company they are before anyone reads the headline.
On turnbull.ca only the word "life" in the headline turns blue, and that same blue comes back on Book a tour. A parent knows exactly where to click without being told.
The quote form sitting right in the Infinity Paving hero, opening with one big residential or commercial choice, is exactly how a paving company should ask for the job.
That oversized loop from the Wanderbrands logo wrapping around the whole van is a great move. The brand looks built to travel before you read a word about it.
Matching the bronze buttons on the Arc & Oak site to the wood in the hero photo makes the interface feel like it came out of the same workshop as the cabinets.
Using the real Express van, phone number and all, as the hero image on the Nampa site is a smart call. A homeowner sees exactly what will pull into their driveway.
Keeping everything lowercase on Elo Coffee, from the wordmark down to the hero line, gives a Shopify store the tone of a small roaster talking to you across the counter.
Congrats on the 2026 Webby for The Wildlife Society. The dark green panel with that italic serif, set over a full bleed wildlife photo, gives a research society a front page with real confidence.
